sources.title: HTTP Semantics
sources.observed_operation: Opened the RFC and inspected ETag weak/strong comparison, If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since precedence, Vary selection fields and 304 semantics.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: If-None-Match uses weak comparison; Last-Modified is implicitly weak except narrow conditions; If-None-Match takes precedence over If-Modified-Since. Vary names request fields that may select a representation, and Vary:* means request syntax alone cannot establish an equivalent later selection.
sources.applicability: Supports correcting the draft's 304 inference and identifies the missing selected-variant key in the checker.

sources.title: HTTP Caching
sources.observed_operation: Opened the RFC and inspected Vary cache-key matching, conditional validation request construction, 304 updates, freshness and disconnected reuse.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: A stored response's Vary-selected request fields must match or be revalidated; an independently initiated validation request is synthesized using the stored method, target and Vary fields. A cache may participate in validation, so a 304 observation does not itself prove direct origin contact.
sources.applicability: Supports variant-aware validator records, the wording correction for the UI, and separation of cache freshness from source version.

sources.title: Web Annotation Data Model
sources.locator: §§ 4.2.4 Text Quote Selector, 4.2.5 Text Position Selector, 4.3 State
sources.observed_operation: Opened the Recommendation and inspected quote normalization/context, code-point position rules, multiple-match behavior, position brittleness and representation State.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Text Quote Selectors may use exact text and prefix/suffix; multiple matches are all matches. Text Position Selector end is exclusive, uses Unicode code points and is brittle under source edits/dynamic content; a State can identify a representation.
sources.applicability: Supports the draft's paired passage selectors and its refusal to silently resolve ambiguity or carry offsets across representations.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.observed_operation: Opened the Recommendation; compared the draft's relation vocabulary with the carried investigator source-map locators and definitions.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: The relations distinguish quoted derivation, revision with substantial retained content, context-specific specialization and alternate aspects; they do not make a redirect equivalent to a revision.
sources.applicability: Supports the draft's typed, evidence-backed source relationships.

sources.title: Git core data model
sources.version: Rolling official documentation; page identifies latest Git manual as 2.56.0, updated 28 September 2026
sources.locator: OBJECTS and REFERENCES sections, especially immutable objects, branches and tags
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official manual and inspected object immutability and ref semantics.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Git objects do not change after creation and IDs hash type/content; branch refs move as commits are added, while tags are usually not changed. A full commit plus repository/path is more exact than a moving branch URL.
sources.applicability: Supports the repository-hosted source alternative and the draft's caveat about tag/version assertions.

sources.title: Getting permanent links to files
sources.version: Rolling official GitHub documentation, accessed 12 October 2026
sources.locator: “Getting permanent links to files”; commit-pinned file links
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official documentation and confirmed GitHub's permalink description for an exact file version.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: GitHub's Y-key permalink records the exact commit version shown; scope is files displayed in GitHub repositories.
sources.applicability: Supports a practical repository-specific source locator, not a general web-document identity.

sources.title: HTTP Framework for Time-Based Access to Resource States (Memento)
sources.observed_operation: Opened the RFC from the carried source index.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: The protocol provides temporal state navigation where implemented; archive coverage, uptime and relation to a vendor product release are not guaranteed.
sources.applicability: Supports the draft's optional archive route and warning against silent substitution.

sources.title: Secure Hash Standard
sources.observed_operation: Opened the NIST publication PDF from the carried source index; detailed digest interpretation remains limited as stated in the investigator's source-map.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: SHA-256 is a specified message-digest algorithm; a digest is a local integrity fingerprint, not a publisher or version assertion.
sources.applicability: Supports the draft's algorithm-tagged local byte fingerprint alongside source identity.

sources.title: Software Heritage persistent identifiers
sources.version: Documentation version 1.6, last modified 30 April 2021 per carried source map; rolling docs URL
sources.locator: Overview, syntax, object types and context/path qualifiers
sources.observed_operation: Attempted direct open; site returned access-denied, matching carried limitation. Did not treat this as full-page independent review.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Only carried indexed text was available for specific v1.6 semantics; identifier scope is software archives, not arbitrary web pages.
sources.applicability: The draft appropriately presents this as an optional, evidence-limited alternative rather than a general identifier.

sources.title: Select best match for quote selectors in PDFs when position-based anchoring fails
sources.locator: Issue description on position-hint page ordering, fuzzy match threshold and early return
sources.observed_operation: Opened the issue and inspected its description and activity.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: The issue concerns PDF.js text-rendering shifts and one anchoring implementation that returned the first sufficiently good match in page order, potentially before a better match on a later page.
sources.applicability: A bounded example of anchor drift and false fuzzy matches; not evidence every selector system shares the bug.

sources.observed_operation: Opened merged PR and pinned implementation/test files; inspected cross-page whitespace-normalized search and exact, whitespace-different, near and context-sensitive cases. Did not run tests.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: PDF.js-specific matching/normalization and performance tradeoff. PR/code inspection does not establish tests pass in the current environment; no test was executed.
sources.applicability: Supports the draft's validation design and carefully bounded issue-to-fix example.
